clue.text: An old Northerner in action as portrayed

indicators.note: the ancient tribesman sits inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish ancestor is shown in the middle of some deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something depicted has been shown or drawn, a synonym of portrayed.

clue.text: Far from sweet about a letter that's stylish

indicators.note: about means the dry wine word goes around the letter

parts.note: dry wine is the opposite of sweet
ess is the spelt name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A sour note in a smart letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and elegant, fit for a formal occasion.

clue.text: One-time alternative for a minister

parts.note: one-time means former, in the past
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A former choice of clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a member of the clergy leading a congregation.

clue.text: Praise lines written in drink

indicators.note: written in means one piece is placed within the word for a drink

parts.note: a cup is a drink, as in a cup of tea
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Toasting someone with lines composed over a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk something up is to extol it, so this phrasal verb means laud.

clue.text: American naval officers sensing mutiny…

indicators.note: a mutiny is a revolt, so the letters of sensing rebel into a new order

explanation.surface: US officers at sea detecting a rebellion brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy.

clue.text: Split about holidays

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
leave is time off work, as holidays are

explanation.surface: A family divided over where to go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split, as with a cleaver or axe.

clue.text: … in America at any rate

parts.note: continues the previous clue as if about the mutiny, but defines an American adverb meaning anyway

explanation.surface: The mutiny happens in the US, anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from 4 down, so the clue seems to finish the mutiny story.
explanation.definitionFit: This chiefly US adverb means at least or anyhow.

clue.text: The right scoffed after a put off

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the letter A

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A right-winger mocked after being snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate is to estrange or repel someone, turning them away.

clue.text: Steady flow when the day's over

parts.note: even means steady or regular
the tide is the flow of the sea

explanation.surface: A calm current at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening.

clue.text: Try first to become a writer

parts.note: an essay is an attempt or try
1st, written out with letters, gives IST

explanation.surface: Advice to an aspiring author: have a go before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is read as the abbreviation 1ST, with the digit 1 looking like the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is someone who writes essays, a kind of author.

clue.text: Remain all at sea-all at sea

indicators.note: all at sea means confused and muddled, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, its six letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone told to stay put is left utterly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase does two jobs in two places: first as the anagram signal on REMAIN, then repeated literally as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine life and marine charts belong to the ocean, so the adjective means oceanic.

clue.text: Little page getting in dope for venomous creatures

indicators.note: getting in means the letter for page is put inside the word for dope

parts.note: a dope or ass is a fool
p is the short form of page

explanation.surface: A young page boy taking drugs among snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Small poisonous snakes such as the Egyptian cobra; the word names those serpents.

clue.text: Check with attendants when there are hold-ups

parts.note: to check something is to halt or stop it
pages are young attendants or servants

explanation.surface: A traffic inspector with assistants, called out whenever there are delays.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppages are interruptions or delays, the same as hold-ups.

clue.text: View that is not irreversible

indicators.note: something that can be turned round and still read the same is the opposite of irreversible

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An opinion that may yet be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a view that can be changed; cryptically, the word reads the same backwards and forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief someone holds, an opinion.

clue.text: The French craft may appear inferior

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of the
SS stands for steamship, a craft on water

explanation.surface: French boats might look second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Less as an adjective means lower in rank or importance, as in no less a person.

clue.text: Lavish without thinking

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: Spending freely without a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish things cost a great deal, so they are costly.

clue.text: Went around dressed in women's clothing

explanation.surface: Someone who walked past wearing a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt is to go round the edge of something; skirted also describes wearing a skirt.

clue.text: Taking over and taking up rugs in error

indicators.note: error says these letters are set down wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Seizing control while clumsily lifting carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurping is seizing power or a position wrongfully.

clue.text: State support

explanation.surface: Government aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain is to assert something firmly; it also means to keep up or provide for.

clue.text: Put on edge

parts.note: reads as made nervous, but means literally given a keen cutting edge, as with a knife

explanation.surface: Made someone nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Honing a blade gives it a fine cutting rim, so the phrase literally describes whetting.

clue.text: Some enormous standard

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A vast benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a usual standard or pattern.

clue.text: An employer in a more prosperous era

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words prosperous era

explanation.surface: A boss operating during boom times.
explanation.definitionFit: One who employs a tool or service uses it, so an employer in this sense is someone who uses it.

clue.text: Like suits?

parts.note: seems to ask about fondness for clothing, but means all the same, as matching outfits are

explanation.surface: A question about enjoying smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical outfits worn by a team are alike, and the word means consistent and unvarying.

clue.text: Sarcastic humour at being taken in by father

indicators.note: the short word goes inside the word for father

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a male parent

explanation.surface: A dad who is the butt of mocking jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses irony and ridicule to mock, a kind of biting wit.

clue.text: A number maybe bite though!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible alternative arrangement of the letters of bite

explanation.surface: Perhaps a figure of bite, after all!
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning even if or although.

clue.text: The rebel leader soon spoke at great length

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: The head of the uprising soon gave a long speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ran on kept talking far too long, an idiom for droning.

clue.text: Restriction 26 put back

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint
the answer to 26 down supplies this piece

explanation.surface: A curb on a market stall being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall is to set up again, returning something to its place.

clue.text: A good man, totally stable

parts.note: St is short for saint, a good man
all means wholly or totally

explanation.surface: A good fellow who is entirely steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a compartment for one animal in a barn, part of a stable.

clue.text: The type with the right inclination

definitions.text: The type with the right inclination

parts.words: The type with the right inclination
parts.note: sounds like a person of sound tendencies, but describes printing letters that slope to the right

explanation.surface: A person with the proper attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanted print leaning rightward is the typeface used for emphasis, a printing term.

clue.text: Present act-original

parts.note: to do is to act
native means original to a place, indigenous

explanation.surface: A performer offering an act that is new.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a gift or donation, a formal word for a present.

clue.text: Terrible danger for a bird

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of danger are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful threat to some bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The male goose is a specific waterfowl, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Hits back in case it's minimal

indicators.note: back tells us the word for hits is read in the other direction

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
lest means for fear that, in case

explanation.surface: Someone retaliating in case it is a tiny matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest amount is the least possible, which is minimal.
